official.question: Is this the official PhotoCraft website?
official.answer: No. PhotoCraft Online is an independent site hosting the open-source WebAssembly build. For the upstream project, visit GitHub and getartcraft.com.

safe.question: Is it safe to use?
safe.answer: Editing runs locally in your browser. We do not upload your images during editing. Download desktop builds from official GitHub Releases.

requirements.question: System requirements?
requirements.answer: Modern desktop browser with WebGPU (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox). First load downloads ~25 MB and may take 30–60 seconds.

psd.question: Can I open PSD files online?
psd.answer: Yes. PhotoCraft supports layered PSD import and export. Still in early alpha — keep backups for critical work.

bugs.question: Something isn't working — what should I do?
bugs.answer: Report issues on the official GitHub repository. This site mirrors the official web build.

desktop.question: How do I get the desktop app?
desktop.answer: Visit our Download page or GitHub Releases for macOS, Windows, and Linux installers.

github.question: Where is the PhotoCraft source code?
github.answer: The official repository is at github.com/storytold/photocraft. Visit our GitHub page for source code, releases, and how this site relates to the upstream project.

hero.title: Download PhotoCraft
hero.subtitle: Free, open-source desktop builds for macOS, Windows, and Linux — or use the editor in your browser.

macos.name: macOS
macos.alternative: Apple Silicon and Intel in one file

steps.1: On GitHub Releases, under Assets, download the file ending in _universal.dmg.
steps.2: Open the .dmg and drag PhotoCraft into your Applications folder.
steps.3: If macOS blocks the app, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

steps.1: On GitHub Releases, under Assets, download the .msi installer (or .zip for portable).
steps.2: Run the installer and follow the setup wizard.
steps.3: Launch PhotoCraft from the Start menu or desktop shortcut.

steps.1: On GitHub Releases, under Assets, download the .AppImage file.
steps.3: Run the AppImage, or install .deb / .rpm if you prefer a package manager.

github.title: How to download from GitHub
github.description: All desktop builds are published on the official GitHub Releases page.

steps.1: Open the PhotoCraft Releases page on GitHub.
steps.3: Scroll down and expand the Assets section.
steps.4: Click the file that matches your platform (see the table below).

developers.title: For developers
developers.description: Self-host the WebAssembly build on your own static hosting (Cloudflare R2, S3, etc.).
developers.web_zip: Download photocraft-web-*.zip from GitHub Releases Assets.
developers.docs: See our R2 setup guide in the project repository docs folder.

browser.q: Do I need to download anything?
browser.a: No. You can use PhotoCraft entirely in your browser at /editor — no install required. First load downloads ~25 MB.

which_file.a: macOS: .dmg · Windows: .msi (or .zip portable) · Linux: .AppImage. When in doubt, use the recommended option on your platform card above.

requirements.a: Desktop: macOS 11+, Windows 10+, or modern Linux. Browser editor: Chrome, Edge, or Firefox with WebGPU; HTTPS required.

safe.a: Only download from github.com/storytold/photocraft/releases or getartcraft.com. Avoid third-party mirrors.

alpha.a: PhotoCraft is in early alpha. Expect bugs — keep backups of important PSD files.
